To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) DB design anomalies degrade the performance of NLIDBs; (b) the performance degradation is due to the ambiguity of the natural language expressions that the NLIDB has to process; (c) the performance degradation can be avoided by (i) designing the NLIDB so that it can handle the ambiguity of the NL expressions, and (ii) designing the NLDB so that it can be queried using NL expressions that do not contain ambiguous NL expressions;
(a) the performance of NLIDBs degrades when accessing DBs with design anomalies, and (b) the performance of an NLIDB can be improved by correcting the design anomaly.
the performance of NLIDBs can be improved by using a DB schema with fewer design anomalies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What is the effect of design anomalies on the performance of NLIDBs?
the design of a NLIDB for querying a DB with design anomalies.
the problem of how to improve the performance of NLIDBs in the case of accessing a DB with design anomalies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of NLIDBs is a good alternative to access information from a DB.

the performance degradation of NL-IDBs due to design anomalies can be reduced if the NLIDBs are able to identify the design anomalies and to use the information provided by the DBMS about them to improve the performance.
the performance of NLIDBs is affected by DB design anomalies and that the best solution for this problem is to design the DB without any anomaly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of a NLIDB must take into account that it could be querying a database with design anomalies.

, in the presence of design anomalies in the DBs to be queried, the NLIDBs' performance (recall) can be improved by: (1) avoiding the use of the NLIDB's default DB access strategy, (2) using a different access strategy, (3) using a DB query rewriting technique, or (4) combining two or more of the above solutions.
the performance of NLIDBs can be improved by using a set of techniques that are described in this paper.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of NLIDBs is affected by design anomalies, and the performance degradation can be avoided by using a combination of techniques. The main contribution
DB design anomalies are not an issue to be ignored by the NLIDB community.
the performance of NLIDBs can be enhanced when they use a DB query plan that takes into account the design anomalies present in the DB.
